texts: The incidence of atrial arrhythmias is reduced after the lateral tunnel procedure: B.
In the old atriopulmonary Fontan the whole right atrium is exposed to venous pressure, dilates and scars, so atrial flutter and other re-entrant arrhythmias are common.
The lateral tunnel, and still more the extracardiac conduit, spare most of the atrium.
Survival after a modern Fontan is around 90 percent at 10 years, thromboembolism affects up to about one in five patients, and ventricular dysfunction has many causes.
In the picture, the pirate and the bunting dance in the old swollen lobby, while the tunnel lobby stays calm.
Memory hook: give the water a tunnel, and the pirate leaves the lobby.
